cards.text: King Hezekiah of Judah has died, and his son Manasseh now reigns in his place (2 Chronicles 32:33). Friend, this new king is YOUNG. When I was brand new on the Millers' counter, they trusted me with one tray of dough, and I still smudged half of it.

cards.question: How old is Manasseh when he becomes king of Judah?
Young king, LONG run. Manasseh reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: Manasseh does evil in the sight of the LORD, following the abominations of the nations the LORD drove out before the Israelites. Friend, that's flipping past every good recipe card to the one with ABOMINATION written across the top and saying, "Ooh, let's make THIS one."

cards.question: Manasseh's father, King Hezekiah, had torn down the high places. Manasseh ___ them.
Along with the high places, Manasseh raises up altars for the Baals and makes Asherah poles.

cards.text: He worships and serves all the host of heaven too.
Then Manasseh builds altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “My Name will remain in Jerusalem forever.” Of ALL the places, friend. Of ALL the places.

cards.question: Manasseh builds altars to all the host of heaven in the LORD's house. Where in it?

cards.text: It gets darker, friend. He sacrifices his sons in the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom.

cards.question: Through all of this, Manasseh stays far away from sorcery, mediums and spiritists.

cards.text: He does great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger. Then he takes the carved image he made and sets it up in the house of God.

cards.question: God had promised King David and his son Solomon He would never again make the Israelites leave their land. But there was a condition. What was it?

answers.text: That they carefully do all He commanded through Moses
That they build Him a bigger and grander temple
That they defeat every nation living around them

cards.question: Manasseh leads Judah and Jerusalem astray. How does their evil compare with the nations the LORD destroyed before the Israelites?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Manasseh and his people, and they don't listen. I ignored a beeping oven timer ONE time, friend, and I'm still scraping that tray.

cards.question: Since Manasseh and his people won't listen, the LORD brings the military commanders of Egypt's king against them.

cards.text: The commanders of Assyria's king capture Manasseh, put a hook in his nose and bind him with bronze shackles.

cards.question: The commanders of Assyria's king take Manasseh away to ___.

cards.text: King Manasseh is a long way from his throne in Jerusalem now, and he is in distress. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I know that spot: when you're that low, there's only one way left to look.

cards.question: In his distress, Manasseh seeks the favor of the LORD his God and earnestly ___ himself before the God of his fathers.

cards.text: Manasseh prays to the LORD. After everything he's done, friend, I bet the whole room is holding its breath.

cards.question: After everything Manasseh has done, the LORD receives his plea and hears his prayer.
The LORD hears Manasseh's plea. Where does the LORD bring him?

answers.text: Back to Jerusalem and his kingdom

cards.question: Back home in Jerusalem, what does Manasseh come to know?

answers.text: That his kingdom will last forever
That Assyria will leave him alone

cards.text: After this, Manasseh rebuilds the outer wall of the City of David, raises it a LOT higher and stations military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah. Friend, I can't stack three cookie boxes without a wobble, and this man is raising a whole city wall.

cards.question: Once the foreign gods and the idol are out of the LORD's house, Manasseh keeps them in his palace.

cards.text: He dumps them outside the city, along with the altars he built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem. Then he restores the altar of the LORD and sacrifices peace offerings and thank offerings on it.

cards.question: With the LORD's altar restored, Manasseh tells the people of Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless, the people of Judah still sacrifice at the high places. To whom do they offer those sacrifices?

answers.text: Only to the LORD their God
To the Baals of the nations
To all the host of heaven

cards.text: Half-fixed, friend, like a cookie that's golden on top and still gooey in the middle. The rest of Manasseh's acts, with his prayer and the words of the seers who spoke to him, are written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
The Records of the Seers keep his prayer too, along with all his sin. Then Manasseh rests with his fathers and is buried at his palace, and his son Amon reigns in his place.
Amon is twenty-two years old when he becomes king of Judah.

cards.question: How long does King Amon reign in Jerusalem?

cards.text: Amon does evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. He serves and sacrifices to all the idols Manasseh made.
But Amon does not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had done. His father's story has two halves, friend, and Amon only follows the FIRST one.

cards.question: Instead of humbling himself, Amon ___ his guilt.

cards.text: Then Amon's servants conspire against him and kill him in his palace. But the people of the land kill all those who conspired against King Amon.

cards.question: Who do the people of the land make king in Amon's place?
